title: The release pipeline is one GitHub Action whose branch picks the channel and whose release_mode picks the semver bump; nobody edits package.json versions or changelogs by hand
content:
`.github/workflows/release-branch.yml` calls `releases/release.ts`, which drives Nx's release tooling. A developer controls exactly two things: **the branch the workflow runs on**, which decides the channel, and **the `release_mode` input**, which decides the semver bump. Nx writes the versions into every workspace `package.json`, generates changelogs, publishes to npm under the channel's dist-tag, pushes a `chore(release): publish <version>` commit and tags `v<version>` — on every run.

| Branch | Channel | npm dist-tag | Version shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | dev | `dev` | `X.Y.Z-dev.N` |
| `release/staging/<label>` | staging | `staging` | `X.Y.Z-staging.N` |
| `release/production/<label>` | production | `latest` | `X.Y.Z` |

The `<label>` is a human hint Nx never parses; the published version comes from the workspace `package.json` plus the mode. Any other branch name makes the script throw. The mode is rewritten per channel:

| Channel | Mode picked | Effective Nx specifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dev / staging | `prerelease` | `prerelease` (preid `dev` / `staging`) |
| dev / staging | `patch` / `minor` / `major` | `prepatch` / `preminor` / `premajor` |
| production | `prerelease` | **rejected — throws** |
| production | `patch` / `minor` / `major` | `patch` / `minor` / `major` |

Prerelease counters start at `.1`, not `.0`. The other workflow inputs (`skip_publish`, `skip_changelog`, `skip_push`, `skip_git_tag`, `skip_stage`, `skip_commit`, `verbose`) are recovery flags for reruns after partial failures; `dry_run` simulates with no side effects. Concurrency is per branch and **queues** rather than cancels. The older `manual-release.yml` ("Full Managed Release") is deprecated. Production is the only channel that also requires updating `RELEASE-NOTES.md` and announcing in `#coredev-releases`.
